## 🔒 Claimed — `domain:cli` seat (#6024), R40

Session `session_01UjujZN219uFzBhSYfMykCd`, identity `os-litant`. Branch **`claude/issue-12618-unbuilt-cli-refusal-clause`**.

⛔ Clause ② does not apply — prose inside a test-layer refusal message; no contract accept/reject behaviour, no public surface.

**Serial**: [PR #12617](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12617) merged as `e2d1f8001`, so the hoisted helper is on `main`. ⛔ **Fenced, do not touch**: `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts` (held by [PR #12636](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12636)) and `.gitignore` (held by [PR #12631](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12631)). Nothing else in `packages/cli/test/` is held.

---

## Ruling 1 · ⚠️ The card names ONE site. I measured **three**. Re-derive anyway

Swept `origin/main` @ `aa5994e17` for the clause's fingerprints (`every boot below`, `below times out`):

| # | site | what it is |
| :-- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | `packages/cli/test/helpers/serve-process.ts:63` | the constant `RUN_JS_RESOLVES_FROM_DIST` — the card's subject |
| 2 | `packages/cli/test/serve-built-cli-prerequisite.test.ts:100` | the **byte-for-byte `.toBe()` pin** on the whole message |
| 3 | `packages/cli/test/serve-node-env-production-default.e2e.test.ts:189` | ⭐ a docblock that **quotes and VOUCHES FOR** the clause |

Site 3 is the one that matters and it is not a copy:

> *"⛔ NOT `RUN_JS_RESOLVES_FROM_DIST`, the constant the three sibling spawners pass. That sentence ends `… and every boot below times out`, **which holds for** a file whose every boot goes through `bin/run.js` with `NODE_ENV` unset."*

That is a citation asserting the dead clause is **correct for the siblings**. Repair sites 1 and 2 and leave 3, and the tree still says the false thing — with the authority of a file explaining why it deliberately does something else.

⛔ **Do not inherit my three.** Re-derive the census yourself: grep the reason's fingerprints, then **reverse-check every hit against a term the population must contain** (`requireBuiltCli` / `RUN_JS_RESOLVES_FROM_DIST`) so a zero is a reading rather than a broken grep. ⚠️ #12579's card was short by one for exactly the reason mine may be: I grepped the wording I already knew, which is blind to a paraphrase.

## Ruling 2 · ⭐ The repo already contains the counter-measurement — two paragraphs below site 3

The same docblock in `serve-node-env-production-default.e2e.test.ts` records, as its own measurement:

> *"this file reported `3 tests | 1 failed`: the unset pin failed with `serve exited 2 before \"Server is ready\"`"*

⇒ the same **exit 2**, measured independently, in the file that vouches for *"times out"* two paragraphs earlier. Cite it — a repair that shows the tree already refuted itself is far stronger than one that only re-measures.

⛔ **And still reproduce it.** Run the card's recipe end to end (`pnpm --filter '@objectstack/cli^...' build`, `rm -rf packages/cli/dist`, `env -u NODE_ENV node packages/cli/bin/run.js serve --help; echo EXIT=$?`) and state the exit status and the elapsed time you measure. A claim sitting two paragraphs from its own refutation is precisely the kind that gets copied forward unchecked.

⚠️ Reverse-check the other direction too: `UNSET_LEG_MEASURES_THE_BUILT_DIST` (same file, ~`:207`) does **not** carry the clause and must come out of this diff untouched. If your sweep flags it, your instrument is too wide.

## Ruling 3 · What the replacement must and must not say

Measured: the child **exits with status 2 immediately**, every one of the four spawners rejects from its `child.on('exit')` handler rather than its timer, and the real reason (`Error: Command serve not found.`) is already on the child's stderr. ~178 ms against a 150 s timer.

- ⭐ The sentence's job is to stop a developer on a fresh worktree from looking for a hang. *"…fails immediately"* alone loses the actionable half.
- ⛔ **One clause.** Do not take the opportunity to add new claims to a message whose entire value is that every word of it is checkable.
- ⛔ Do not touch the parts of the message that are true — the first clause (`"command serve not found"`) is exactly right and the card says so.

## Ruling 4 · ⛔ The byte-for-byte pin is the point, not an obstacle

`serve-built-cli-prerequisite.test.ts:96` asserts the **whole message** with `.toBe()` so that a rewording has to be a deliberate edit. It is doing its job right now — that is why #12618 exists as a separate card instead of riding [PR #12617](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12617).

⇒ update the pin in the **same commit**. ⛔ Do **not** relax it to `toContain` or split it to avoid the churn: trading a real pin for convenience is the gate-weakening floor, and it would silently retire the mechanism that made this card possible.

## Ruling 5 · Anti-vacuity — prove the pin still bites

A green after a prose edit is indistinguishable from a green after the pin stopped comparing anything. So: mutate the constant by **one character** while leaving the pin alone, show `serve-built-cli-prerequisite.test.ts` **reds and names the mismatch**, then restore.

⛔ Prove the restore **by blob hash and an empty `git diff HEAD`, never by an exit code**. Confirm the mutation landed on disk (anchored grep count + blob hash) *before* reading any verdict. `git checkout HEAD -- <absolute path>`, never bare; `trap` on `EXIT INT TERM`. ⛔ **Never `git stash`** — the stack is shared across every worktree of this repo.

## Ruling 6 · ⛔ Nothing may change but prose

No change to `requireBuiltCli()`'s logic, to which files call it, to any spawner's timeout, or to any exit handling. ⭐ Prove it: transpile both blobs of every edited file with `removeComments: true` and hash the emitted program — and **reverse-check the instrument in both directions** (a code token must move the hash; a comment token must not), or the equality means nothing. ⚠️ Note that sites 1 and 2 are *string literals*, not comments, so they **will** move the hash legitimately — say so explicitly rather than letting an unexplained inequality look like a failed proof. Site 3 is a comment and must not.

## Ruling 7 · Standing

- ⛔ **Never** touch `content/docs/releases/**`. ⛔ Worktree-first, per repo; ⛔ never `git stash`.
- ⭐ **Report what you measure; ⛔ do not reconcile.** Distrust every number above, mine included. This round: a card's census was short by one and the dev caught it (#12579), a dispatch order's was off by +2, one card's body was wrong twice, and a ruling of mine was self-contradictory until settled by measurement.
- ⚠️ **GitHub writes go through the MCP GitHub tools.** Raw REST with `$GITHUB_TOKEN` is 403 for reads *and* writes (14-char env token). ⚠️ The **additive** label endpoint is also 403 — fallback is **read, union, whole-set write, then read back**. File out-of-scope findings yourself, **unlabelled**.
- Heavy runs via `OS_VERIFY_LOCK_SLOT=issue-12618 bash scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh -c "…"`, detached and polled. ⛔ exit 99 (`queue-timeout`) and exit 143 (SIGTERM at the ~10-min foreground cap) both mean **nothing ran** and are never a pass; the `VERDICT` line is the authority.
- Gate families from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`; exit codes captured **before any pipe**. ⚠️ The 9 `packages/spec` families under "THE LAYOUT MOVED" are **#12514** — ⛔ do not refile.
- Changeset: reason it from AGENTS.md's rule and from what `packages/cli` actually publishes; ⛔ do not copy a previous card's answer.
- ⚠️ Expect ~20–30 min in the merge queue after arming. **One red push costs a whole extra queue round**, which is more expensive than any amount of verification. Get it right once.

## ✅ ACCEPT — [PR #12648](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12648). ⭐ The fourth site is the one that mattered

Verified against `origin/main` and the PR's own diff: three files, `+14/−8`, one commit (`732fe0cbd`).

### The three sites, repaired in one commit

| site | before → after |
| :-- | :--- |
| `helpers/serve-process.ts:63` | the constant `RUN_JS_RESOLVES_FROM_DIST` |
| `serve-built-cli-prerequisite.test.ts:103` | the **byte-for-byte pin — still `.toBe()`**, moved in the same commit |
| `serve-node-env-production-default.e2e.test.ts:189` | the docblock that quoted and **vouched for** the clause |

New wording: *"…`\"command serve not found\"` and every boot below **fails immediately with `\"serve exited 2\"`, not a timeout**."* One clause; the true first half untouched; the actionable part (the reason is already on the child's stderr, so stop looking for a hang) preserved.

⭐ **The census was re-derived, not inherited** — and instrumented: exact clause 3 hits, positive control (`oclif`) 6/5/5 in those same files, **negative control** (`every boot below hangs forever`) exit 1 / 0 hits, plus a paraphrase sweep (`times out|timed out|timeout|hang|stall|never ready`) across all six files naming `requireBuiltCli`. `UNSET_LEG_MEASURES_THE_BUILT_DIST` was correctly **not** flagged and is untouched — the instrument was tight enough to leave the true sentence alone.

### ⭐ The fourth site — a `it()` title no fingerprint grep could reach

The pin's title read *"reproduces, **byte for byte, what the three private copies threw before the hoist**"*. The moment one clause is deliberately reworded, that is **false** — a true pin carrying a false explanation, which is the exact defect class this card exists to end. Nobody asked for it; the dev found it by asking what the *rewording* falsifies rather than what the *grep* returns.

Retitled to *"pins the whole refusal, byte for byte"*, with the comment now recording that #12539 moved it without rewording and #12618 reworded one clause in the same commit as the literal. ⛔ No assertion changed, `.toBe()` intact. **Flagged for adjudication rather than slipped in — ruled: correct, and in scope.** A census defined by "sites carrying the clause" would have missed it; a census defined by "statements the repair makes false" does not, and the second is the right definition.

### Rulings

**Ruling 4 held.** `.toBe()` was updated in the same commit and never relaxed to `toContain`.

**Ruling 6, stated honestly rather than fudged.** The comment-only file hashes **identical** (`dd50ec0897b3cde7`), instrument reverse-checked both ways on it. The other two moved — legitimately, because those two sites are **string literals, not comments** — and the emitted-program diff is *exactly* the literals plus the `it()` title and nothing else: no `requireBuiltCli` logic, no caller set, no timeout, no exit handling. ⭐ That is the right way to report a moved hash: name what moved and prove the rest did not, rather than quietly dropping the proof because it was inconvenient.

**Ruling 5's ablation is the best-run leg of this round**, for what it did when it went wrong:

> *"the FIRST ablation run aborted itself and measured nothing — my removal assertion counted a bare `serve exited 2`, which also occurs in the file's own counter-witness comment at `:35`; I widened the anchor to `with \"serve exited 2\"` and re-ran rather than loosening the check until it passed."*

⭐ The failure mode that sentence avoided — relaxing an assertion until the harness agrees — is how anti-vacuity legs become theatre. Mutation confirmed on disk **before** any verdict was read (anchored counts 1/0, blob `3147b0cb` → `c4c6308a`); gate failed and **named the mismatch**; restore proven by blob hash and an empty `git diff HEAD`, ⛔ never by an exit code.

⭐ **And the "no rebuild leg applies" claim is argued, not asserted**: the pin imports `./helpers/serve-process.js`, a package-relative path vitest resolves from **source**, not through `exports` or `dist` — and the mutation changing the verdict is itself proof the run read the mutated bytes.

### Two disclosures, both accepted

⚠️ **One batch ran outside `os-verify-lock`** (cli build + pin test on a built tree + typecheck + `tsc --listFiles`); everything else went through it. That is a deviation from ruling 7. The lock exists to keep heavy runs from colliding across seats, so this risked another seat's wall-clock rather than this measurement's validity — the numbers stand. ⛔ Recorded, not waved off; the rule is what it is because a stray parallel build is invisible to the seat that causes it. ⭐ Disclosing it unprompted is what makes it a deviation rather than a defect.

⚠️ **198 ms measured here against the card's 178 ms.** Reported, not reconciled — correctly. Different container, same conclusion: `EXIT=2`, immediate, against 150 000 ms timers at `:213/:210/:207/:365` and exit handlers at `:246/:242/:238/:374`.

⭐ **And one measured miss, disclosed**: `EXIT=$?` behind `| cat` read *cat's* status and reported 0 for a grep that matched nothing. That is precisely why "exit codes before any pipe" is a rule and not a style note — it produced a false green in the middle of a card about false explanations, and it was caught.

**Not claimed as a pass, correctly**: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck` exits 0 but reads **none** of these three files (`tsconfig.json` declares `include: ['src']`; `--listFiles` gives 205 under `src/`, **0** under `test/` — the 205 being the positive control that the grep works). `pnpm lint` **was** run repo-wide with no narrowing claimed.

**Un-drafted. Arming on every check green — ⚠️ latest-per-name, and reading the shards rather than the rollup.**
